title: His father's dance band and how he composed
summary: Love says his father's band played dances and lancers and rags, and describes how he dreamed up pieces and had them scored.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did he play any fun with his band?

No, he didn't have no fun with Ron. He used to play for dancers mostly. And I tell you, he had to swell all because they used to sit down and make their own music. Just make up most of the whole program, the stuff they made up. And he used to have some dancers at that time. Quadrillion and lances. And he used to play shatters and zilting. And I said variety. And two steps, one steps. He used to play little rags too, and then he used to play sentimental music in the overtill. My father was a first class musician. You know what he could do? What's that? Just go to sleep at night like that sometimes, thinking about music and dream up, dream a piece. And he'd get up at two o'clock, every time in the morning, get his horn right away and play it. Keep from forgetting to play it and then he'd score it down, you know. Man, he'd get up the next day and play it. And my mother used to be his witness, you know, how that sounds kid? She said, that sounds lovely. She said, but it looked like it ought to have another part. Now see, you've got two parts, you ought to have three parts. That's a pretty novel. She said, I ought to be named, she'd give it a name too, you know. It ought to be named like something, some kind of flower or something like that. He'd get that down, he'd write it, write the lead of it, you know, and then he'd bring it around to Norrie Barber's house. And Norrie Barber was something like Seal, you know, he could score that stuff down, you know. He'd write the guitar part and the bandage, the guitar and the bass. Clarence William Paul was playing bass with him, Dennis William. He died up young building not so long ago. Just fix me to go see Clarence. He was working for the teepee railroad company.
